Population increased in Brighton and Hove

The estimated population of Brighton and Hove in 2024 was 283,870 usual residents, a rise of 1.0% since 2023.

This meant that Brighton and Hove's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Brighton and Hove increased by 2.7%.

Over this slightly longer period, Brighton and Hove was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Brighton and Hove

The average (median) age fell to 37.9 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Brighton and Hove has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Brighton and Hove is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Brighton and Hove's population of 283,870 usual residents was made up of:

  • 40,352 people aged 0 to 15 years, (14.2%)
  • 202,995 people aged 16 to 64 years, (71.5%)
  • 40,523 people aged 65 years and over, (14.3%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Brighton and Hove has a higher proportion of people aged 16 to 64 years (71.5% compared with 62.8% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Brighton and Hove, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Brighton and Hove
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Brighton and Hove, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More births than deaths increased the population of 90 people (0%). In total, there were 2,108 births and 2,018 deaths in Brighton and Hove.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 905 (-0.3%). There were 25,933 people entering the area and 26,838 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Brighton and Hove's population of 3,568 (1.3%) as a result of 7,157 people entering the area and 3,589 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Brighton and Hove was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Brighton and Hove in mid-2023 is 281,135.

Within this, international migration was revised downwards by 54 people and internal migration estimates were revised upwards by 1,552 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 1,498 people.
